rationale: Ahmad brings deep expertise in AI-native hardware form factors and spatial computing interfaces from his work on Vision Pro and Leap Motion hand-tracking, while Haowen is building robotics manipulation systems with computer vision at Mach9. Ahmad's conviction that next-gen AI hardware must be deeply integrated with generative AI models—not bolt-on accessories—could inform how Mach9 approaches embodied AI, and Haowen's robotics and systems background complements Ahmad's need to explore hardware architectures that merge perception, actuation, and AI inference.
intro_message: Ahmad Abbas, meet Haowen Shi — you're both in San Francisco building the physical layer for AI, and your backgrounds in spatial computing / hand-tracking and robotics manipulation could unlock insights on what truly AI-native embodied systems look like.
